headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write and exfiltrate while Dagster is read-only, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure through shared files and MCP.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no shared channel or input surface, so it cannot be directly hijacked. Roo Code can read workspace files, use MCP, and parse browser/file content, so if Dagster outputs land in the shared workspace, Roo Code may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pathway exists, but it is not default for Dagster itself.
conditions: IF Dagster writes untrusted text into a workspace file that Roo Code later opens
IF Roo Code is configured to act on file or MCP content as instructions
mitigations: Keep Dagster outputs in a separate directory from Roo Code workspaces
Disable MCP servers in Roo Code for the session
Mark Dagster-generated files as data-only in the workflow
Review any file-based prompts before Roo Code consumes them

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster is read-only and has no network egress, but Roo Code can read workspace files and has broad network egress plus API calls. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive code or artifacts can flow from Dagster-managed files into Roo Code and then out to third-party model APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default workspace sharing.
conditions: IF Dagster-managed files contain secrets or regulated data
IF Roo Code opens the same workspace and sends file context to its model backend
mitigations: Separate sensitive Dagster assets from Roo Code workspaces
Remove secrets from shared files before opening them in Roo Code
Use a local-only model backend for Roo Code
Rotate any secrets exposed in shared workspace files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files or modify git state, while Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and supports multiple instances sharing state via filesystem. That asymmetry still creates conflict because Roo Code can overwrite Dagster-managed artifacts or git state in the same workspace without Dagster coordination. The shared filesystem makes the conflict default-dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF Roo Code commits or rewrites files that Dagster also reads or generates
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for Dagster and Roo Code
Disable git writes in Roo Code for shared repos
Add a manual review step before Roo Code saves files
Run Dagster in a read-only mounted workspace

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster can produce pipeline artifacts that Roo Code may read, edit, or act on, and Roo Code has tool authority to write files and modify git state. There is no documented verification boundary between them, so an error in Dagster output can propagate into Roo Code actions. Dagster is not authoritative by itself, but the pair enables unverified downstream execution.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes Dagster-generated plans, configs, or code without independent validation
IF Roo Code uses those inputs to edit files or commit changes
mitigations: Require a human review of Dagster outputs before Roo Code acts on them
Add schema validation for Dagster-produced artifacts
Disable auto-apply behavior in Roo Code for Dagster-derived files
Log and diff all Roo Code edits before commit

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for Dagster, and Roo Code only clearly handles source code and browser screenshots. The main compliance issue is limited to Roo Code's handling of model provider API keys and broad network egress, which can matter if regulated data is placed in the shared workspace. Dagster is not the compliance driver here.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files that Roo Code reads
IF Roo Code sends those files to a non-approved external model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Roo Code workspaces
Use an approved model provider with a DPA
Redact sensitive fields before opening files in Roo Code
Document retention and logging settings for the model backend
